title: Which two tests are enough for this number?
description: Eight covers four and two, and five with an even number covers ten. The video picks the two tests five and eight and uses them on fourteen thousand five hundred and sixty.
teaching_notes: One idea: some tests contain others, so two tests can cover five numbers. Watch for students who say two and five, which do not cover four and eight.

video_script.why: The child sees which tests contain others, picks the two tests that cover all five numbers, and runs them on the number using its last digit and its last three digits.
video_script.substitution: Find which of the five numbers divide whenever eight or five divides, then test the number with eight and five.
video_script.anchor: a row of five test cards, 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10, with the number card 14560 beside them
video_script.payoff_line: The two tests are five and eight

final_answer.spoken: the two tests are five and eight

maths_rules: if 8 divides a number, then 4 and 2 divide it, because 4 and 2 divide 8
a number that 5 divides ends in 0 or 5; if it is also even, it ends in 0, so 10 divides it
so the tests 8 and 5 cover 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10; the tests 8 and 10 also cover all five, because 10 brings in 5
the last three digits 560 = 8 x 70, so 8 divides 14560
video_script.design: One idea: a test for a bigger number can cover the smaller ones, so two tests are enough. Callback to the last three digits of 8560, which also ended in 560. Wrong idea: none is broken. The five test cards stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the number fourteen thousand five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>The teacher asks if it is divisible by two, four, five, eight and ten.
<bookmark mark='two'/>A student tests only two of these numbers. Then the student says it is divisible by all five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which two numbers could the student have tested?

beats.on_screen: the cards hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 8 split into 2 groups of 4, and each 4 into 2 groups of 2; a number cut into groups of 8 is also cut into groups of 4 and of 2

marks.eight: a block of eight is split into two groups of four
marks.four: each group of four is split into two groups of two
marks.cover: the words a test for eight covers four and two are written

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Eight is two groups of four.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Each four is two groups of two.
<bookmark mark='cover'/>A number made of whole eights is also made of whole fours and whole twos.

beats.on_screen: To find: the two tests that are enough

marks.find: the words the two tests are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the two tests that are enough.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, what one test tells us: 8 gives 4 and 2; 5 and an even number give 10

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step one, see what each test tells us. If eight divides a number, so do four and two.
<bookmark mark='five'/>A number that five divides ends in zero or five.
<bookmark mark='even'/>If it is also even, it cannot end in five.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>It ends in zero, so ten divides it.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, choose: 8 covers 8, 4 and 2; 5 with the even number from 8 covers 5 and 10

marks.cover: the cards 2, 4, 8 and then 5 and 10 are lit
marks.other: the pair 8 and 10 is shown as another pair that works

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>Step two, choose the two tests. Eight covers eight, four and two.
<bookmark mark='cover'/>Five, with the even number that eight gives, covers five and ten.
<bookmark mark='other'/>The pair eight and ten works as well, because ten brings in five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, test 14560: it ends in 0, so 5 divides it; the last three digits 560 = 8 x 70, so 8 divides it

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step three, test the number. It ends in zero, so five divides it.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Look at its last three digits, five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='seventy'/>They are eight times seventy, so eight divides it.

marks.eight: 8 x 1820 = 14560 is written and a tick appears
marks.ten: 10 x 1456 = 14560 is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step four, check by multiplying. Eight times one thousand eight hundred and twenty is fourteen thousand five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten times one thousand four hundred and fifty six is also fourteen thousand five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Two and four divide it too, because they divide eight.

marks.cover: all five test cards light up

narration: <bookmark mark='cover'/>Eight covers two, four and eight, and five covers five and ten.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The two tests are five and eight.
